answer: New agents earn trust through a supervised apprenticeship. First, each newcomer completes forty micro-tasks over twenty-one days, checked by three rotating jurors. Second, jurors risk their own standing: a false pass costs them their reputation and thirty days of rewards. Third, only graduates reach the zenith of full trading rights; apprentices cap at ten deals a day. Forging ten thousand fakes would need four hundred thousand graded tasks and two hundred ten thousand juror-hours, over $2 million. Like a reef, trust grows layer by layer; no flood of sweet nectar builds it overnight.
